date_enacted.from: Not enacted; public hearing held 2025-09-24 and withdrawal resolution adopted 2025-11-19
date_enacted.to: Not enacted. Public hearing held 2025-09-24; the Town Board's resolution withdrawing the proposed moratorium (Local Law #7 of 2025) is confirmed on the November 19, 2025 Town Board meeting agenda (Item 4, Motions and Resolutions: "Resolution Withdrawing Proposed Moratorium (Local Law #7 of 2025)").
date_enacted.reason: Town of Lansing's own Municode meeting-agenda system confirms the withdrawal resolution's date and title directly.

outcome.from: Moratorium proposal withdrawn. Lansing ZBA later treated the proposed high-performance-computing data center as a permitted use under existing industrial/research zoning; local groups filed an Article 78 challenge.
outcome.to: Moratorium proposal withdrawn November 19, 2025. The Lansing Zoning Board of Appeals ruled on December 23, 2025 that the proposed AI/HPC data center is a permitted "general processing" use under existing industrial/research zoning; Cayuga Lake Action Now (CLEAN) and FLX Strong filed an Article 78 petition in NY State Supreme Court on January 30, 2026 against the Lansing ZBA and TeraWulf challenging that ruling. The outcome of the Article 78 petition was not confirmed as of this pass (2026-07-31); the last located update was an April 14, 2026 report on a separate state water-permit approval for the associated power plant, which could not be accessed this pass due to source rate-limiting.
outcome.reason: Ithaca Voice's coverage (individually fetched articles dated 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-30) confirms the sequence of events after the withdrawal.

new_candidates.jurisdiction: State of New York (Executive Order, not a local-government action)
new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-14, Executive Order No. 62 signed by Governor Kathy Hochul
new_candidates.duration: Up to one year; freezes new state permitting for data centers >=50 MW while DEC/DPS conduct an environmental impact review
new_candidates.trigger: Statewide concern over rapid data-center growth and grid/environmental impacts
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-07-14; applies only to state permitting and explicitly does not override local-government permitting or zoning
new_candidates.affected_projects: Reportedly affects roughly 20 hyperscale data center projects statewide, including TeraWulf's approximately 400 MW Cayuga Data Campus in the Town of Lansing
new_candidates.outcome: Governor Hochul signed a one-year freeze on new state permitting for data centers of 50 MW or more pending an environmental impact review by DEC/DPS

evidence.title: TeraWulf, data center face new hurdle as Hochul issues executive order
evidence.supports: Describes Executive Order 62's scope, duration, and effect on the TeraWulf Lansing project

evidence.title: Hochul signs executive order on data center permitting
evidence.supports: Corroborates the one-year duration and 50 MW threshold of Executive Order 62
evidence.quote: New York will lead the way in creating the strongest standards in the nation for data center development.

new_candidates.notes: This is a state-level executive action (the Governor), not a local-government moratorium, so it sits outside this dataset's normal scope -- included because it directly affects NY data-center coverage and post-dates the 2026-04-28 cutoff. Both sources are news; the official Executive Order text (e.g., on governor.ny.gov) was not directly fetched this pass. Recommend locating the primary EO text before treating this as a firm database entry.
